purpose: Tavaborole is used to treat a fungal infection of the toenails called onychomycosis. It helps clear up nails that have become thick, discolored, or brittle because of a fungus. You apply it directly to the affected toenail so it works right where the problem is.
how_it_works: Tavaborole works by blocking a special tool the fungus needs to make proteins and survive. Without that tool, the fungus cannot grow or spread, and it eventually dies off. Think of it like cutting off the fungus's food supply so it slowly goes away.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects happen right at the nail area and include mild redness, flaking, peeling, or slight irritation around the nail or nearby skin. These are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use tavaborole in or near your eyes, mouth, or vagina — it is only meant for the toenails. If you develop severe skin irritation, a rash, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling or trouble breathing, stop using it and contact your doctor right away. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medication.
typical_dosing: You apply a small amount of the solution to the entire surface of the affected toenail once a day, usually at bedtime. Make sure the nail is clean and dry before applying. Treatment usually lasts 48 weeks, so patience is important — nail infections take a long time to fully clear up.
